contract tests\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Planned behavior\\r\\n\\r\\nThe app will accept PDF, TXT, Markdown, DOCX, and CSV files during a session. Each successful upload set will get an isolated, ephemeral Chroma collection. The user will ask questions against the active set and see answers with cited source passages. Replacing the set will switch retrieval to the new collection without code changes. Restarting the app will discard the in-memory index, so files must be uploaded again.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Parsing API\\r\\n\\r\\n`parse_documents` accepts a list of `UploadedDocument` values and returns one `ParsedDocument` per source. Supported extensions are `.pdf`, `.txt`, `.md`, `.markdown`, `.docx`, and `.csv`. Each document contains ordered `ParsedElement` values with a stable source ID, source filename, element type, page number when available, and the current section title. Table elements keep Unstructured's HTML and extracted header cells when available. CSV uses its first row as headers; DOCX tables retain their text and HTML structure, but headers are only labeled when the source structure identifies them.\\r\\n\\r\\n```python\\r\\nfrom document_rag.models import UploadedDocument\\r\\nfrom document_rag.parsing import parse_documents\\r\\n\\r\\ndocuments = parse_documents([\\r\\n    UploadedDocument(filename=\\\"notes.md\\\", content=b\\\"# Notes\\\\n\\\\nA fact.\\\"),\\r\\n    UploadedDocument(filename=\\\"memo.txt\\\", content=b\\\"Another fact.\\\"),\\r\\n])\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nThe validator rejects unsupported extensions, empty or whitespace-only files, non-UTF-8 TXT/Markdown/CSV files, duplicate filenames, and uploads over the configured file count or byte limit. A file that yields no usable elements is rejected after parsing. Files are processed in memory; extracted elements remain grouped by source.\\r\\n\\r\\nSee [PLAN.md](PLAN.md) for the detailed implementation sequence, evaluation approach, and limitations.\\r\\n\\r\\n## References\\r\\n\\r\\n- [Gemini 3.8 Flash model](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-3.8-flash)\\r\\n- [Gemini Embedding 2 model](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-embedding-2)\\r\\n- [LangChain Chroma integration](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain-chroma/vectorstores/Chroma)\\r\\n- [Unstructured package and extras](https://pypi.org/project/unstructured/)\\r\\n\"}}\n{\"status\":\"fulfilled\",\"value\":\"unstructured/unstructured/chunking/title.py at main · Unstructured-IO/unstructured · GitHub (https://github.com/Unstructured-IO/unstructured/blob/main/unstructured/chunking/title.py)\\nciteturn10search0 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: last week; Table elements keep Unstructured's HTML and extracted header cells when available. CSV uses its first row as headers; DOCX tables retain their text and HTML structure, but headers are only labeled when the source structure identifies them.\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom document_rag.models import UploadedDocument\r\nfrom document_rag.parsing import parse_documents\r\n\r\ndocuments = parse_documents([\r\n    UploadedDocument(filename=\"notes.md\", content=b\"# Notes\\n\\nA fact.\"),\r\n    UploadedDocument(filename=\"memo.txt\", content=b\"Another fact.\"),\r\n])\r\n```\r\n\r\nThe validator rejects unsupported extensions, empty or whitespace-only files, non-UTF-8 TXT/Markdown/CSV files, duplicate filenames, and uploads over the configured file count or byte limit. A file that yields no usable elements is rejected after parsing. Files are processed in memory; extracted elements remain grouped by source.\r\n\r\n## Chunking API\r\n\r\nPass parsed documents to `chunk_documents` to get bounded `DocumentChunk` values. The new collection becomes ready before the old collection is deleted. If building fails, the old index remains available. Each collection is isolated and lost when the Python process exits; no Chroma persistence directory is used.\r\n\r\n## Retrieval API\r\n\r\n`retrieve` searches the active index and returns the top K `RetrievalResult` values. Retrieval does not call the answer model.\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom document_rag.retrieval import retrieve\r\n\r\nresults = retrieve(\"What does the report say about sales?\", index)\r\nfor result in results:\r\n    print(result.rank, result.source, result.page, result.text)\r\n```\r\n\r\nPass `top_k=...` for a one-call override, or set `TOP_K` in `.env`. It labels the supplied passages `[S1]`, `[S2]`, and so on, then asks Gemini Flash for a Pydantic response with `answer`, `evidence_ids`, and `insufficient_evidence`. It rejects unknown or inconsistent IDs and maps valid IDs to the source filename, page, section, chunk ID, and passage text supplied by retrieval. +"""UI lifecycle tests without Gemini or a real Chroma collection."""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace

+
+
+def _parsed(name: str) -> ParsedDocument:
+    return ParsedDocument(
+        source_id=name,
+        source_name=name,
+        elements=[
+            ParsedElement(
+                element_id=f"{name}:0",
+                source_id=name,
+                source_name=name,
+                text="Annual leave is 20 days.",
+                category="NarrativeText",
+                page_number=2,
+                section_title="Leave",
+            )
+        ],
+    )
+
+
+def _chunk(name: str) -> DocumentChunk:
+    return DocumentChunk(
+        chunk_id=f"{name}:chunk",
+        source_id=name,
+        source_name=name,
+        text="Leave: Annual leave is 20 days.",
+        embedding_text="Leave: Annual leave is 20 days.",
+        page_number=2,
+        heading="Leave",
+    )
+
+
+def test_ui_build_ask_replace_and_reset(monkeypatch) -> None:
+    indexes = []
+    deleted = []
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(ui, "load_config", lambda: SimpleNamespace(require_google_api_key=lambda: "fake"))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(ui, "parse_documents", lambda uploads, config: [_parsed(item.filename) for item in uploads])
+    monkeypatch.setattr(ui, "chunk_documents", lambda parsed, config: [_chunk(item.source_name) for item in parsed])
+
+    def fake_build(chunks, *, config, previous_index):
+        index = SimpleNamespace(chunk_count=len(chunks), ready=True, name=f"index-{len(indexes)}")
+        indexes.append(index)
+        if previous_index is not None:
+            previous_index.ready = False
+            deleted.append(previous_index.name)
+        return index
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(ui, "build_index", fake_build)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(ui, "is_index_ready", lambda index: bool(index and index.ready))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(ui, "reset_index", lambda index: (deleted.append(index.name), setattr(index, "ready", False)))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        ui,
+        "retrieve",
+        lambda question, index, config: [
+            RetrievalResult(
+                rank=1,
+                chunk_id="policy.txt:chunk",
+                text="Leave: Annual leave is 20 days.",
+                source="policy.txt",
+                page=2,
+                section="Leave",
+                distance=0.1,
+            )
+        ],
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        ui,
+        "generate_answer",
+        lambda question, results, config: GroundedAnswer(
+            answer="Annual leave is 20 days [S1].",

+            citations=[
+                AnswerCitation(
+                    evidence_id="S1",
+                    chunk_id=results[0].chunk_id,
+                    source=results[0].source,
+                    page=results[0].page,
+                    section=results[0].section,
+                    text=results[0].text,
+                )
+            ],
+        ),
+    )
+
+    app = AppTest.from_file("app.py", default_timeout=30).run()
+    assert not app.exception
+    assert app.button(key="Ask").disabled
+    app.file_uploader[0].upload("policy.txt", b"Annual leave is 20 days.", "text/plain").run()
+    app.button(key="Build Index").click().run()
+    assert not app.exception
+    assert app.session_state.active_index is indexes[0]
+    assert app.session_state.active_filenames == ["policy.txt"]
+
+    app.text_input(key="question").set_value("How much leave?").run()
+    assert not app.button(key="Ask").disabled

+    assert app.button(key="Ask").disabled
+    assert app.session_state.active_index is None
+    assert app.session_state.chunks == []
+    assert deleted == ["index-0", "index-1"]

Replace the document set and rebuild; old answers are cleared and retrieval switches to the new dataset. Delete the superseded in-memory collection after successful replacement; provide a reset action.\r\n\r\n## Pipeline\r\n\r\nUpload -> validate size/type -> partition into typed Unstructured elements -> form structure-aware text chunks -> embed their text with Gemini -> store vectors and compact source metadata in Chroma.\r\n\r\nQuestion -> embed -> retrieve top five chunks -> supply labeled evidence and question to Gemini -> validate response and citation IDs -> render answer and source passages.\r\n\r\nKeep title/section context with nearby prose. Keep a small table with its heading, headers, and units in one chunk. If a table must be split, repeat its heading and column headers with each row group. Do not pass table chunks through a generic text splitter. Start with prose chunks around 400 words and 60-word overlap, preserving page attribution; tune after inspecting actual extraction and retrieval examples. Embeddings are created from each chunk's textual representation, not from raw layout or table objects. Charts/images need separate extraction or description and remain outside the initial scope.\r\n\r\n### Chunking optimization\r\n\r\nUse Unstructured's `by_title` chunking as the first candidate: keep section boundaries, preserve table elements, and carry document title plus heading path into the text embedded for each chunk. Keep the original extracted text and source metadata for citations. Apply a bounded chunk-size policy and small prose overlap; let large tables form table chunks, checking that headers and context remain available. Avoid splitting an element just to meet an arbitrary target when that would break a row or sentence.\r\n\r\nCompare at least two configurations on a small, fixed question set drawn from two unlike documents: (1) plain bounded text chunks and (2) structure-aware chunks with contextual heading/title prefixes. Record whether the correct source enters top-k retrieval, whether answers cite the right passage, indexing time, and chunk count. Select the simpler approach unless the enhanced approach clearly helps.\r\n\r\nTrue **late chunking** encodes a longer text first and pools contextualized token vectors into chunk vectors afterward. Gemini's public embedding API returns an embedding for each input, not the token-level vectors needed to perform that pooling. Therefore the Gemini/Chroma implementation will not claim to implement late chunking. If a later comparison justifies it, it would require a suitable long-context embedding model or service and a separate compatibility and cost check. Contextual heading/title prefixes are a practical optimization here, but they are not late chunking.\r\n\r\n## Grounding and reliability\r\n"

+"""Small, rule-based RAG evaluation over a fixed local document set."""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import re
+from collections.abc import Callable, Sequence
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, model_validator
+
+from document_rag.chunking import chunk_documents
+from document_rag.generation import generate_answer
+from document_rag.models import GroundedAnswer, RetrievalResult, UploadedDocument
+from document_rag.parsing import parse_documents
+from document_rag.retrieval import retrieve
+from document_rag.vector_store import VectorIndex, build_index, reset_index
+
+
+DEFAULT_FIXTURE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "evaluation" / "cases.json"
+_INLINE_ID = re.compile(r"\\[(S[1-9]\\d*)\\]")
+
+
+class EvaluationCase(BaseModel):
+    """Expected evidence for one question; keywords must occur in one passage."""
+
+    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)
+
+    question: str = Field(min_length=1)
+    expected_source: str | None = None
+    expected_page: int | None = Field(default=None, ge=1)
+    expected_keywords: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
+    answerable: bool
+
+    @model_validator(mode="after")
+    def validate_expected_evidence(self) -> "EvaluationCase":
+        if self.answerable and (not self.expected_source or not self.expected_keywords):
+            raise ValueError("Answerable cases need an expected source and keywords.")
+        if not self.answerable and (self.expected_source or self.expected_page or self.expected_keywords):
+            raise ValueError("Unanswerable cases must not declare expected evidence.")
+        if any(not word.strip() for word in self.expected_keywords):
+            raise ValueError("Expected keywords must not be blank.")
+        return self
+
+
+class EvaluationSuite(BaseModel):
+    """Local corpus filenames and their questions."""
+
+    documents: list[str] = Field(min_length=1)
+    cases: list[EvaluationCase] = Field(min_length=1)
+
+
+class CaseResult(BaseModel):
+    """Measured retrieval and optional answer checks for one case."""
+
+    question: str
+    answerable: bool
+    expected_source: str | None
+    source_in_top_k: bool | None
+    source_rank: int | None
+    correct_result_rank: int | None
+    hit_at_k: bool | None
+    valid_citations: bool | None = None
+    citations_refer_to_retrieved: bool | None = None
+    insufficient_evidence_correct: bool | None = None
+    answer_contains_expected_keywords: bool | None = None
+
+
+class EvaluationReport(BaseModel):
+    top_k: int = Field(ge=1)
+    cases: list[CaseResult]
+    retrieval_hits: int
+    retrieval_cases: int
+    hit_at_k: float | None
+    valid_citation_cases: int | None
+    abstention_cases_passed: int | None
+    answer_cases: int
+
+
+def load_suite(path: Path = DEFAULT_FIXTURE) -> tuple[EvaluationSuite, list[UploadedDocument]]:
+    """Read a trusted local fixture and its document files."""
+    suite = EvaluationSuite.model_validate_json(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    documents = [
+        UploadedDocument(filename=name, content=(path.parent / name).read_bytes())
+        for name in suite.documents
+    ]
+    return suite, documents
+
+
+def _correct_passage(case: EvaluationCase, result: RetrievalResult) -> bool:
+    return (
+        result.source == case.expected_source
+        and (case.expected_page is None or result.page == case.expected_page)
+        and all(word.casefold() in result.text.casefold() for word in case.expected_keywords)
+    )
+
+
+def _answer_checks(
+    case: EvaluationCase, answer: GroundedAnswer, results: Sequence[RetrievalResult]
+) -> dict[str, bool]:
+    unique_results = list(dict.fromkeys(result.chunk_id for result in results))
+    by_chunk = {result.chunk_id: result for result in results}
+    id_to_chunk = {f"S{position}": chunk_id for position, chunk_id in enumerate(unique_results, 1)}
+    inline_ids = set(_INLINE_ID.findall(answer.answer))
+    declared_ids = set(answer.evidence_ids)
+    citation_ids = {citation.evidence_id for citation in answer.citations}
+    valid_citations = (
+        len(answer.evidence_ids) == len(declared_ids)
+        and len(answer.citations) == len(citation_ids)
+        and declared_ids == citation_ids == inline_ids
+        and all(evidence_id in id_to_chunk for evidence_id in declared_ids)
+    )
+    citations_refer_to_retrieved = all(
+        citation.evidence_id in id_to_chunk
+        and citation.chunk_id == id_to_chunk[citation.evidence_id]
+        and citation.chunk_id in by_chunk
+        and citation.source == by_chunk[citation.chunk_id].source
+        and citation.page == by_chunk[citation.chunk_id].page
+        and citation.section == by_chunk[citation.chunk_id].section
+        and citation.text == by_chunk[citation.chunk_id].text
+        for citation in answer.citations
+    )
+    if case.answerable:
+        valid_citations = valid_citations and not answer.insufficient_evidence and bool(declared_ids)
+    else:
+        valid_citations = valid_citations and answer.insufficient_evidence and not declared_ids
+    return {
+        "valid_citations": valid_citations,
+        "citations_refer_to_retrieved": citations_refer_to_retrieved,
+        "insufficient_evidence_correct": answer.insufficient_evidence == (not case.answerable),
+        "answer_contains_expected_keywords": (
+            all(word.casefold() in answer.answer.casefold() for word in case.expected_keywords)
+            if case.answerable
+            else answer.insufficient_evidence
+        ),
+    }
+
+
+def evaluate_cases(
+    cases: Sequence[EvaluationCase],
+    index: VectorIndex,
+    *,
+    top_k: int = 5,
+    retrieval_fn: Callable[..., list[RetrievalResult]] = retrieve,
+    answer_fn: Callable[..., GroundedAnswer] | None = generate_answer,
+) -> EvaluationReport:
+    """Run fixed questions; no judge model or semantic grading is used."""
+    if not cases:
+        raise ValueError("Provide at least one evaluation case.")
+    if top_k < 1:
+        raise ValueError("top_k must be positive.")
+    rows: list[CaseResult] = []
+    for case in cases:
+        results = retrieval_fn(case.question, index, top_k=top_k)[:top_k]
+        matching_sources = [
+            result.rank for result in results if result.source == case.expected_source
+        ] if case.answerable else []
+        matching_passages = [
+            result.rank for result in results if _correct_passage(case, result)
+        ] if case.answerable else []
+        checks = (
+            _answer_checks(case, answer_fn(case.question, results), results)
+            if answer_fn is not None
+            else {}
+        )
+        rows.append(
+            CaseResult(
+                question=case.question,
+                answerable=case.answerable,
+                expected_source=case.expected_source,
+                source_in_top_k=bool(matching_sources) if case.answerable else None,
+                source_rank=min(matching_sources) if matching_sources else None,
+                correct_result_rank=min(matching_passages) if matching_passages else None,
+                hit_at_k=bool(matching_passages) if case.answerable else None,
+                **checks,
+            )
+        )
+    answerable_rows = [row for row in rows if row.answerable]
+    answer_rows = [row for row in rows if row.valid_citations is not None]
+    hits = sum(row.hit_at_k is True for row in answerable_rows)
+    return EvaluationReport(
+        top_k=top_k,
+        cases=rows,
+        retrieval_hits=hits,
+        retrieval_cases=len(answerable_rows),
+        hit_at_k=hits / len(answerable_rows) if answerable_rows else None,
+        valid_citation_cases=(
+            sum(row.valid_citations and row.citations_refer_to_retrieved for row in answer_rows)
+            if answer_rows else None
+        ),
+        abstention_cases_passed=(
+            sum(row.insufficient_evidence_correct is True for row in answer_rows if not row.answerable)
+            if answer_rows else None
+        ),
+        answer_cases=len(answer_rows),
+    )
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Evaluate the local sample RAG corpus.")
+    parser.add_argument("--cases", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_FIXTURE)
+    parser.add_argument("--top-k", type=int, default=5)
+    parser.add_argument("--retrieval-only", action="store_true")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    suite, documents = load_suite(args.cases)
+    index = build_index(chunk_documents(parse_documents(documents)))
+    try:
+        report = evaluate_cases(
+            suite.cases,
+            index,
+            top_k=args.top_k,
+            answer_fn=None if args.retrieval_only else generate_answer,
+        )
+        print(report.model_dump_json(indent=2))
+    finally:
+        reset_index(index)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
*** End Patch`));

False\r\n# Document RAG\r\n\r\nA local Streamlit application that builds a retrieval index from documents uploaded at runtime and answers questions with source citations.\r\n\r\n## Stack\r\n\r\n- Python 3.11â€“3.13 and Streamlit\r\n- LangChain with `langchain-google-genai` for Gemini and `langchain-chroma` for Chroma\r\n- `gemini-embedding-2` for embeddings, configured for 768-dimensional vectors\r\n- `gemini-3.8-flash` for answers\r\n- Unstructured for PDF, TXT, Markdown, DOC, DOCX, and CSV parsing\r\n- Pydantic for configuration and pipeline data; pytest for tests; python-dotenv for `.env`\r\n- Chroma collections held in memory only, with no persistence directory\r\n\r\nThe model IDs are configurable. Access and quota depend on the API key's Google project. Tests use fake embeddings and mocked chat responses; they make no Gemini API calls.\r\n\r\n## Setup\r\n\r\nUse Python 3.12 if available. On Windows PowerShell:\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\npy -3.12 -m venv .venv\r\n.\\.venv\\Scripts\\Activate.ps1\r\npython -m pip install --upgrade pip\r\npython -m pip install -r requirements.txt\r\nCopy-Item .env.example .env\r\n```\r\n\r\nSet `GOOGLE_API_KEY` in `.env` before building an index with Gemini embeddings. The model variables and `TOP_K` in `.env` may be changed without editing code. `TOP_K` defaults to 5. PDF parsing uses Unstructured's high-resolution strategy to detect tables and may download local layout models or require native PDF tools. Scanned pages without extractable text are reported as an error.\r\n\r\nLegacy DOC parsing requires LibreOffice (`soffice`) on PATH. DOCX does not require LibreOffice. Run the app and tests:\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\nstreamlit run app.py\r\npython -m pytest\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Project map\r\n\r\n```text\r\napp.py                    Streamlit entry point\r\ndocument_rag/\r\n  config.py               .env loading and validated settings\r\n  models.py               shared Pydantic contracts\r\n  parsing.py              Upload validation and Unstructured extraction\r\n  chunking.py             section-aware prose and table chunking\r\n  embeddings.py           Gemini embedding adapter\r\n  vector_store.py         in-memory Chroma lifecycle and search\r\n  retrieval.py            question-to-evidence retrieval\r\n  generation.py           grounded Gemini answers and citation validation\r\n  ui.py                   Streamlit interface and debug views\r\ntests/                    credential-free contract tests\r\nevaluation/               local synthetic documents and question expectations\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Using the app\r\n\r\nUpload PDF, TXT, Markdown, DOC, DOCX, or CSV files in the sidebar and select **Build Index**. Enter a question and select **Ask** to see a grounded answer, citations, and supporting passages. Expand **Debug** to inspect parsed elements, chunks, retrieved passages, cosine distances, and source metadata.\r\n\r\nChanging the selected files disables questions until **Build Index** succeeds. A successful rebuild creates a fresh collection and deletes the previous one; if it fails, the previous collection remains available when its files are selected again. **Reset** deletes the active collection and clears answer and debug data. Session state keeps the index across reruns; restarting the app or losing the browser session discards it.\r\n\r\n## Parsing API\r\n\r\n`parse_documents` accepts a list of `UploadedDocument` values and returns one `ParsedDocument` per source. Supported extensions are `.pdf`, `.txt`, `.md`, `.markdown`, `.doc`, `.docx`, and `.csv`. Each document contains ordered `ParsedElement` values with a stable source ID, source filename, element type, page number when available, and the current section title. Table elements keep Unstructured's HTML and extracted header cells when available. CSV uses its first row as headers; Word tables retain their text and HTML structure when Unstructured provides it.\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom document_rag.models import UploadedDocument\r\nfrom document_rag.parsing import parse_documents\r\n\r\ndocuments = parse_documents([\r\n    UploadedDocument(filename=\"notes.md\", content=b\"# Notes\\n\\nA fact.\"),\r\n    UploadedDocument(filename=\"memo.txt\", content=b\"Another fact.\"),\r\n])\r\n```\r\n\r\nThe validator rejects unsupported extensions, empty or whitespace-only files, non-UTF-8 TXT/Markdown/CSV files, duplicate filenames, and uploads over the configured file count or byte limit. A file that yields no usable elements is rejected after parsing. Extracted elements remain grouped by source. Legacy DOC conversion may use temporary files inside Unstructured.\r\n\r\n## Chunking API\r\n\r\nPass parsed documents to `chunk_documents` to get bounded `DocumentChunk` values. Prose is grouped within each section and page using Unstructured's `by_title` chunker. Each chunk's text includes its section heading, and the same text is available as `embedding_text`. Tables are kept separate; their headers are repeated when rows span multiple chunks. Chunk IDs are deterministic for a source and do not depend on the order of other uploaded files.\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom document_rag.chunking import chunk_documents\r\n\r\nchunks = chunk_documents(documents)\r\n```\r\n\r\nDefaults are a 2,000-character hard limit, 1,400-character target, and 80-character minimum used to rebalance short trailing prose. A standalone short fact is kept rather than discarded. Title-only documents and inputs exceeding the configured 200-chunk limit raise `ChunkingError`.\r\n\r\n## Vector index API\r\n\r\n`build_index` creates a new collection in `chromadb.EphemeralClient()` and stores each chunk's text plus its source, page, heading, type, and ID metadata. The embedding adapter uses `GoogleGenerativeAIEmbeddings` with `gemini-embedding-2`. Search returns ranked `RetrievedChunk` values; distances are vector distances, not confidence scores.\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom document_rag.vector_store import build_index, is_index_ready, reset_index, search_index\r\n\r\nindex = build_index(chunks)\r\nif is_index_ready(index):\r\n    hits = search_index(index, \"What does the document say?\", top_k=5)\r\nreset_index(index)\r\n```\r\n\r\nTo replace a dataset, call `build_index(new_chunks, previous_index=index)`. The new collection becomes ready before the old collection is deleted. If building fails, the old index remains available. Each collection is isolated and lost when the Python process exits; no Chroma persistence directory is used.\r\n\r\n## Retrieval API\r\n\r\n`retrieve` searches the active index and returns the top K `RetrievalResult` values. Each result includes rank, chunk ID, text, source filename, page and section when available, element type, and cosine distance. A smaller distance indicates a closer vector match; it is not an answer-confidence score. Retrieval does not call the answer model.\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom document_rag.retrieval import retrieve\r\n\r\nresults = retrieve(\"What does the report say about sales?\", index)\r\nfor result in results:\r\n    print(result.rank, result.source, result.page, result.text)\r\n```\r\n\r\nPass `top_k=...` for a one-call override, or set `TOP_K` in `.env`. Empty questions and missing or reset indexes produce clear errors.\r\n\r\n## Answer generation API\r\n\r\n`generate_answer` takes a question and retrieved results; it does not perform retrieval. It labels the supplied passages `[S1]`, `[S2]`, and so on, then asks Gemini Flash for a Pydantic response with `answer`, `evidence_ids`, and `insufficient_evidence`. It rejects unknown or inconsistent IDs and maps valid IDs to the source filename, page, section, chunk ID, and passage text supplied by retrieval. Gemini does not provide citation metadata to the final result.\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom document_rag.generation import generate_answer\r\nfrom document_rag.retrieval import retrieve\r\n\r\nresults = retrieve(\"How much annual leave is provided?\", index)\r\nanswer = generate_answer(\"How much annual leave is provided?\", results)\r\n```\r\n\r\nWith no retrieved evidence, or when Gemini says the evidence is insufficient, the function returns a standard abstention. Citation validation confirms that IDs refer to supplied passages; it cannot by itself prove every sentence is factually supported.\r\n\r\nSee [PLAN.md](PLAN.md) for the detailed implementation sequence, evaluation approach, and limitations.\r\n\r\n## Evaluation\r\n\r\nThe local [question fixture](evaluation/cases.json) pairs three synthetic documents with four answerable questions and one unanswerable question. Each answerable case specifies its source filename, optional page, and keywords expected together in a retrieved passage.\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\npython -m document_rag.evaluation --retrieval-only\r\npython -m document_rag.evaluation\r\n```\r\n\r\nBoth commands build a fresh in-memory index from the fixture and need a working Gemini embedding key. The second also calls Gemini Flash for answers. The runner prints JSON with each question's source presence in top K, source rank, first passage rank matching source/page/keywords, and hit@k; it then reports aggregate hit@k. For answers it checks inline citation IDs, their mapped chunk IDs and metadata against retrieved results, expected abstention, and literal answer keywords. Unanswerable questions have no retrieval hit expectation because a vector search still returns nearby passages. These rule-based checks do not establish semantic correctness. Tests in `tests/test_evaluation.py` use doubles and require no API key. You can change `--top-k` or point `--cases` to another local fixture with the same schema.\r\n\r\n## References\r\n\r\n- [Gemini 3.8 Flash model](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-3.8-flash)\r\n- [Gemini Embedding 2 model](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-embedding-2)\r\n- [LangChain Chroma integration](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain-chroma/vectorstores/Chroma)\r\n- [Unstructured package and extras](https://pypi.org/project/unstructured/)\r\n\n{'streamlit': '1.65.0', 'langchain': '1.4.3', 'langchain-google-genai': '4.4.0', 'langchain-chroma': '1.1.0', 'chromadb': '1.5.9', 'unstructured': '0.27.16', 'pydantic': '2.13.5'}\r\n"

## 319. Assistant

```text
The core imports and constructor arguments match the installed LangChain, Chroma, Streamlit, and Unstructured versions. I found one UI issue to fix: a Pydantic validation error can include uploaded file bytes in its string form. I’m making the UI show only the safe error message, and I’m adding a test that a failed rebuild leaves the previous index intact.
```

+## Architecture
+
+\`\`\`text
+Upload → Pydantic validation → Unstructured elements → by_title chunks
+       → Gemini embeddings → ephemeral Chroma collection
+Question → explicit top-K retrieval → Gemini Flash answer
+         → validated evidence IDs → trusted citation metadata + passages
+\`\`\`
+
+The Streamlit UI stores the active index, parsed elements, chunks, and latest answer in session state. Building a replacement set creates a new collection before retiring the old one. Retrieval only searches the active collection, so old and new documents do not mix. Core pipeline steps stay outside \`app.py\`.
+
+## Supported formats
+
+PDF (\`.pdf\`), UTF-8 TXT (\`.txt\`), Markdown (\`.md\`, \`.markdown\`), Word (\`.doc\`, \`.docx\`), and CSV (\`.csv\`). Upload up to 10 files per set, each up to 10 MiB; the resulting set is limited to 200 chunks by default. PDF page numbers are kept when Unstructured provides them. PDF table detection uses its high-resolution strategy and may download layout models or require local PDF tools. Legacy DOC requires LibreOffice; scanned PDFs need extractable text or suitable local OCR support.

Legacy DOC requires LibreOffice; scanned PDFs need extractable text or suitable local OCR support.\r\n\r\n## Project map\r\n\r\n```text\r\napp.py                    Streamlit entry point\r\ndocument_rag/\r\n  config.py               .env loading and validated settings\r\n  models.py               shared Pydantic contracts\r\n  parsing.py              Upload validation and Unstructured extraction\r\n  chunking.py             section-aware prose and table chunking\r\n  embeddings.py           Gemini embedding adapter\r\n  vector_store.py         in-memory Chroma lifecycle and search\r\n  retrieval.py            question-to-evidence retrieval\r\n  generation.py           grounded Gemini answers and citation validation\r\n  evaluation.py           rule-based local evaluation runner\r\n  ui.py                   Streamlit interface and debug views\r\ntests/                    credential-free contract tests\r\nevaluation/               local synthetic documents and question expectations\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Using the app\r\n\r\nUpload PDF, TXT, Markdown, DOC, DOCX, or CSV files in the sidebar and select **Build Index**. Enter a question and select **Ask** to see a grounded answer, citations, and supporting passages. Expand **Debug** to inspect parsed elements, chunks, retrieved passages, cosine distances, and source metadata.\r\n\r\nChanging the selected files disables questions until **Build Index** succeeds. A successful rebuild creates a fresh collection and deletes the previous one; if it fails, the previous collection remains available when its files are selected again. **Reset** deletes the active collection and clears answer and debug data. Session state keeps the index across reruns; restarting the app or losing the browser session discards it.\r\n\r\n## Parsing API\r\n\r\n`parse_documents` accepts a list of `UploadedDocument` values and returns one `ParsedDocument` per source. Supported extensions are `.pdf`, `.txt`, `.md`, `.markdown`, `.doc`, `.docx`, and `.csv`. Each document contains ordered `ParsedElement` values with a stable source ID, source filename, element type, page number when available, and the current section title. Table elements keep Unstructured's HTML and extracted header cells when available. CSV uses its first row as headers; Word tables retain their text and HTML structure when Unstructured provides it.\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom document_rag.models import UploadedDocument\r\nfrom document_rag.parsing import parse_documents\r\n\r\n"

+

+

+    return next(item for item in app.button if item.label == label)
+
+
+def check(app: AppTest, stage: str) -> None:
+    if app.exception:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"{stage}: Streamlit exception: {app.exception[0].message}")
+    if app.error:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"{stage}: UI error: {app.error[0].message}")

I’m making the UI show a specific, safe message for this response, then I’ll retry the UI flow with another configured Gemini Flash model without changing your `.env`.

 def _validation_message(error: ValidationError) -> str:
     """Show validation messages without echoing uploaded bytes from Pydantic input."""
     return "; ".join(str(item["msg"]) for item in error.errors(include_input=False))
+
+
+def _service_error_message(error: Exception, fallback: str) -> str:
+    """Translate common Gemini API status codes without exposing request details."""
+    cause: BaseException | None = error
+    while cause is not None:
+        code = getattr(cause, "code", None)
+        if code == 503:
+            return "Gemini is temporarily busy (503). Try again shortly or configure another Flash model."
+        if code == 429:
+            return "Gemini quota or rate limit reached (429). Try again later or check your quota."
+        cause = cause.__cause__
+    return fallback

+    from unstructured_client import UnstructuredClient

+        pdf_infer_table_structure=suffix == ".pdf",
+    )

After you sign up, you are automatically signed in to your new Unstructured Starter account, at https://platform.unstructured.io.\n\n# Python SDK\n\nOpen in ChatGPT\n\nThe Unstructured Python SDK client allows you to send one file at a time for processing by the Unstructured Partition Endpoint. To use the Python SDK, you’ll first need to set an environment variable named `UNSTRUCTURED_API_KEY`, representing your Unstructured API key. To get your API key, do the following:\n\n  1. If you do not already have an Unstructured account, sign up for free. After you sign up, you are automatically signed in to your new Unstructured Starter account, at https://platform.unstructured.io.\n\nTo sign up for a Team or Enterprise account instead, contact Unstructured Sales, or learn more.\n\n  2. If you have an Unstructured Starter or Team account and are not already signed in, sign in to your account at https://platform.unstructured.io.\n\nFor an Enterprise account, see your Unstructured account administrator for instructions, or email Unstructured Support at support@unstructured.io.\n\n  3. Get your Unstructured API key:\na. After you sign in to your Unstructured Starter account, click API Keys on the sidebar.\n\nFor a Team or Enterprise account, before you click API Keys, make sure you have selected the organizational workspace you want to create an API key for. Each API key works with one and only one organizational workspace. Learn more.\n\nb. Click Generate API Key.\nc. Follow the on-screen instructions to finish generating the key.\nd. Click the Copy icon next to your new key to add the key to your system’s clipboard. If you lose this key, simply return and click the Copy icon again.\n\n\nInstallation\n\nBefore using the SDK to interact with Unstructured, install the library:\n\nPython\n    \n    `pip install unstructured-client\n    `\n\nThe SDK uses semantic versioning and major bumps could bring breaking changes. It is advised to pin your installed version. See the migration guide, later on this page, for breaking change announcements.\n\nBasics\n\nLet’s start with a simple example in which you send a PDF document to the Unstructured Partition Endpoint to be partitioned by Unstructured.\n\nPython\n    \n    `import os, json\n    \n    import unstructured_client\n    from unstructured_client.models import operations, shared\n    \n    client = unstructured_client.UnstructuredClient(\n        api_key_auth=os.getenv(\"UNSTRUCTURED_API_KEY\")\n    )\n    \n    filename = \"PATH_TO_INPUT_FILE\"\n    \n    req = operations.PartitionRequest(\n        partition_parameters=shared.PartitionParameters(\n            files=shared.Files(\n                content=open(filename, \"rb\"),\n                file_name=filename,\n            ),\n            strategy=shared.Strategy.VLM,\n            vlm_model=\"gpt-4o\",\n            vlm_model_provider=\"openai\",\n            languages=['eng'],\n            split_pdf_page=True,            # If True, splits the PDF file into smaller chunks of pages.\n            split_pdf_allow_failed=True,    # If True, the partitioning continues even if some pages fail.\n            split_pdf_concurrency_level=15  # Set the number of concurrent request to the maximum value: 15.\n        ),\n    )\n    \n    try:\n        res = client.general.partition(\n            request=req\n        )\n        element_dicts = [element for element in res.elements]\n        \n        # Print the processed data's first element only.\n        print(element_dicts[0])\n    \n        # Write the processed data to a local file.\n        json_elements = json.dumps(element_dicts, indent=2)\n    \n        with open(\"PATH_TO_OUTPUT_FILE\", \"w\") as file:\n            file.write(json_elements)\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(e)\n    `\n\nAsync partitioning\n\nThe Python SDK also has a `partition_async`. This call is equivalent to `partition` except that it can be used in a non blocking context. For instance, `asyncio.gather` can be used to concurrently process multiple files inside of a directory hierarchy, as demonstrated here:\n\nPython\n    \n    `import asyncio\n    import os\n    import json\n    import unstructured_client\n    from unstructured_client.models import shared\n    \n    client = unstructured_client.UnstructuredClient(\n        api_key_auth=os.getenv(\"UNSTRUCTURED_API_KEY\")\n    )\n    \n    async def call_api(filename, input_dir, output_dir):\n### \n\n​\n\nRetries\n\nYou can also change the defaults for retries through the `retry_config`* parameter when initializing the client. If a request to the API fails, the client will retry the request with an exponential backoff strategy up to a maximum interval of one minute. The function keeps retrying until the total elapsed time exceeds `max_elapsed_time`*, which defaults to one hour. However, you can override these defaults, for example as follows:\n\nPython\n    \n    `# ...\n    from unstructured_client.utils import RetryConfig, BackoffStrategy\n    \n    client = UnstructuredClient(\n        api_key_auth=os.getenv(\"UNSTRUCTURED_API_KEY\")\n        retry_config=RetryConfig(\n            strategy=\"backoff\",\n            retry_connection_errors=True,\n            backoff=BackoffStrategy(\n                initial_interval=500,     # 0.5 seconds: 500 milliseconds\n                max_interval=60000,       # 1 minute: 60 seconds * 1000 milliseconds\n                exponent=1.5,\n                max_elapsed_time=900000,  # 15 minutes: 15 * 60 seconds * 1000 milliseconds\n    `http_client = requests.Session()\n    http_client.verify = False\n    \n    client = UnstructuredClient(\n        client=http_client,\n        ...\n    )\n    `\n\n\nHandling the response\n\nThe partition response defaults to a dict format that can be converted to Unstructured elements with the `elements_from_dicts` utility function as seen below. Otherwise, the API response can be sent directly to your vector store or another destination.\n\nPython\n    \n    `from unstructured.staging.base import elements_from_dicts\n    \n    # ...\n    \n    if res.elements is not None:\n        elements = elements_from_dicts(response.elements)\n    `\n\nParameters & examples\n\nThe parameter names used in this document are for the Python SDK, which follow snake_case convention. The JavaScript/TypeScript SDK follows camelCase convention. Other than this difference in naming convention, the names used in the SDKs are the same across all methods.\n\n  * Refer to the API parameters page for the full list of available parameters.\n  * Refer to the Examples page for some inspiration on using the parameters.\n\n\nMigration guide\n\nThere are breaking changes beginning with Python SDK version 0.26.0. If you encounter any errors when upgrading, please find the solution below. If you see the error: `AttributeError: 'PartitionParameters' object has no attribute 'partition_parameters'` Before 0.26.0, the SDK accepted a `PartitionParameters` object as input to the `sdk.general.partition` function. Beginning with 0.26.0, this object must be wrapped in a `PartitionRequest` object. The old behavior was deprecated in 0.23.0 and removed in 0.26.0.\n    \n    `# Instead of:\n    from unstructured_client.models import shared\n    \n    req = shared.PartitionParameters(\n        files=files,\n    )\n    \n    resp = s.general.partition(\n        request=req\n    )\n    \n    # Switch to:\n    from unstructured_client.models import shared, operations\n    \n    req = operations.PartitionRequest(\n        partition_parameters=shared.PartitionParameters(\n            files=files,\n        )\n    )\n    \n    resp = s.general.partition(\n        request=req\n    )\n    `\n\nIf you see the error: `TypeError: BaseModel.__init__() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given` Beginning with 0.26.0, the `PartitionRequest` constructor no longer allows for positional arguments. You must specify `partition_parameters` by name.\n    \n    `# Instead of:\n    req = operations.PartitionRequest(\n        shared.PartitionParameters(\n            files=files,\n        )\n    )\n    \n    # Switch to:\n    req = operations.PartitionRequest(\n        partition_parameters=shared.PartitionParameters(\n            files=files,\n        )\n    )\n    `--------------------------------------------------------------------------------\nGitHub - Unstructured-IO/unstructured-python-client: A Python client for the Unstructured Platform API · GitHub (https://github.com/Unstructured-IO/unstructured-python-client)\nciteturn21search1 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: 4 days ago; Unstructured-IO / unstructured-python-client Public ... .github  | .github  |    | ... Unstructured Transform quickly turns your files into structured data to feed to your apps, databases, vector stores, AI tools, and agents. Transform is available as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. MCP is an industry standard for connecting AI tools to apps and data sources.\nL31: The Transform MCP server enables you to link your AI tools to Transform. You can then use your AI tools to have Transform ingest your local files and output the results as partitioned, enriched, chunked, and embedded data, ready for your immediate use. The Unstructured **Transform** web URL (\`transform.unstructured.io/api/v2\`) is a different product endpoint and does not work with the Partition API client.

## 629. Assistant

```text
The upload error comes from a missing **Tesseract executable**. The Python wrapper is installed, but Tesseract is not on PATH.

I updated [parsing.py](D:/Projects/Document-RAG/document_rag/parsing.py) so text-based PDFs retry with Unstructured’s `fast` strategy; scanned PDFs now get a clear OCR setup error. The UI warns when that fallback may reduce table extraction. **64 tests pass**, including a real text-PDF extraction test.

I stored the supplied key in the ignored `.env`, but left hosted parsing inactive. The key returned **401** from the Partition API, and the URL you supplied is for [Unstructured Transform](https://docs.unstructured.io/transform/overview), not the separate [Partition API](https://docs.unstructured.io/platform-api/partition-api/sdk-python). A user-scope Tesseract install was also unavailable. For scanned PDFs, install Tesseract with the Windows installer or an elevated `winget install --id UB-Mannheim.TesseractOCR --exact`, then restart Streamlit.
```

Though there have been on-going eï¬€orts to improve reusability and simplify deep learning (DL) model development in disciplines like natural language processing and computer vision, none of them are optimized for challenges in the domain of DIA. This represents a major gap in the existing toolkit, as DIA is central to academic research across a wide range of disciplines in the social sciences and humanities. This paper introduces LayoutParser, an open-source library for streamlining the usage of DL in DIA research and applica- tions. The core LayoutParser library comes with a set of simple and intuitive interfaces for applying and customizing DL models for layout de- tection, character recognition, and many other document processing tasks. To promote extensibility, LayoutParser also incorporates a community platform for sharing both pre-trained models and full document digiti- zation pipelines. Content type: text/html; Source: open({\"ref_id\":\"https://docs.unstructured.io/platform-api/partition-api/sdk-python\",\"lineno\":null}); Redirected to URL: https://docs.unstructured.io/api-reference/legacy-api/partition/sdk-python; Total lines: 366\nL0: > ## Documentation Index\nL1: >\nL2: > Fetch the complete documentation index at: cite0†/llms.txt L3: >\nL4: > Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.\nL5: \nL6: cite1†iframe†www.googletagmanager.com cite2†Skip to main content L7: \nL8: cite3†Unstructured home page Pipelines\nL9: \nL10: Search...\nL11: \nL12: Navigation\nL13: \nL14: Python SDK\nL15: \nL16: cite4†Get started cite5†Core functions cite6†SDK & API cite7†Build pipelines cite8†Deploy & enterprise cite9†General reference L17: # Python SDK\nL18: \nL19: Learn how to install and use the Unstructured Python SDK to send files to the Partition Endpoint, with async partitioning, PDF splitting, and retries.\nL20: \nL21: Open in ChatGPT\nL22: The following information applies to the legacy Unstructured Partition Endpoint.Unstructured recommends that you use the cite10†local-file processing jobs functionality in the cite11†Unstructured Pipelines operations instead. Unstructured’s local-file processing jobs provide many benefits over the legacy Unstructured Partition Endpoint, including support for:\nL23:   * Production-level usage.\nL24:   * Multiple local input files in batches.\nL25:   * The latest and highest-performing models.\nL26:   * Post-transform enrichments.\nL27:   * All of Unstructured’s chunking strategies.\nL28:   * The generation of vector embeddings.\nL29: The Unstructured API also provides support for processing files and data in remote locations.\nL30: The cite12†Unstructured Python SDK†github.com client allows you to send one file at a time for processing by the cite13†Unstructured Partition Endpoint . To use the Python SDK, you’ll first need to set an environment variable named `UNSTRUCTURED_API_KEY`, representing your Unstructured API key. To get your API key, do the following:\nL31:   1. If you do not already have an Unstructured account, cite14†sign up for free†unstructured.io . After you sign up, you are automatically signed in to your new Unstructured Let’s Go account, at cite15†https://platform.unstructured.io†platform.unstructured.io .\nL32: \nL33: To sign up for a Business account instead, cite16†contact Unstructured Sales†unstructured.io , or cite17†learn more .\nL34:   2. If you have an Unstructured Let’s Go, Pay-As-You-Go, or Business SaaS account and are not already signed in, sign in to your account at cite15†https://platform.unstructured.io†platform.unstructured.io .\nL35: \nL36: For other types of Business accounts, see your Unstructured account administrator for sign-in instructions, or cite18†request support .\nL37: \nL38:   3. Get your Unstructured API key:\nL39: a. After you sign in to your Unstructured Let’s Go, Pay-As-You-Go, or Business account, click API Keys on the sidebar.\nL40: For a Business account, before you click API Keys, make sure you have selected the organizational workspace you want to create an API key for. Each API key works with one and only one organizational workspace. cite19†Learn more .\nL41: \nL42: b. Click Generate API Key.\nL43: c. Follow the on-screen instructions to finish generating the key.\nL44: d. Click the Copy icon next to your new key to add the key to your system’s clipboard. If you lose this key, simply return and click the Copy icon again.\nL45: ##\nL46: \nL47: cite20†​ L48: \nL49: Installation\nL50: \nL51: Before using the SDK to interact with Unstructured, install the library:\nL52: \nL53: Python\nL54: \nL55:     `pip install \"unstructured-client>=0.46.2\"\nL56:     `\nL57: \nL58: The SDK uses semantic versioning and major bumps could bring breaking changes. It is advised to pin your installed version. See the cite21†migration guide , later on this page, for breaking change announcements.\nL59: ##\nL60: \nL61: cite22†​ L62: \nL63: Basics\nL64: \nL65: Let’s start with a simple example in which you send a PDF document to the Unstructured Partition Endpoint to be partitioned by Unstructured.\nL66: Python\nL67: \nL68:     `import os, json\nL69: \nL70:     import unstructured_client\nL71:     from unstructured_client.models import operations, shared\nL72: \nL73:     client = unstructured_client.UnstructuredClient(\nL74:         api_key_auth=os.getenv(\"UNSTRUCTURED_API_KEY\")\nL75:     )\nL76: \nL77:     filename = \"PATH_TO_INPUT_FILE\"\nL78: \nL79:     req = operations.PartitionRequest(\nL80:         partition_parameters=shared.PartitionParameters(\nL81:             files=shared.Files(\nL82:                 content=open(filename, \"rb\"),\nL83:                 file_name=filename,\nL84:             ),\nL85:             strategy=shared.Strategy.VLM,\nL86:             vlm_model=\"gpt-4o\",\nL87:             vlm_model_provider=\"openai\",\nL88:             languages=['eng'],\nL89:             split_pdf_page=True,            # If True, splits the PDF file into smaller chunks of pages.\nL90:             split_pdf_allow_failed=True,    # If True, the partitioning continues even if some pages fail.\nL91:             split_pdf_concurrency_level=15  # Set the number of concurrent request to the maximum value: 15.\nL92:         ),\nL93:     )\nL94:     try:\nL95:         res = client.general.partition(\nL96:             request=req\nL97:         )\nL98:         element_dicts = [element for element in res.elements]\nL99: \nL100:         # Print the processed data's first element only.\nL101:         print(element_dicts[0])\nL102: \nL103:         # Write the processed data to a local file.\nL104:         json_elements = json.dumps(element_dicts, indent=2)\nL105: \nL106:         with open(\"PATH_TO_OUTPUT_FILE\", \"w\") as file:\nL107:             file.write(json_elements)\nL108:     except Exception as e:\nL109:         print(e)\nL110:     `\nL111: ##\nL112: \nL113: cite23†​ L114: \nL115: Async partitioning\nL116: \nL117: The Python SDK also has a `partition_async`. This call is equivalent to `partition` except that it can be used in a non blocking context. For instance, `asyncio.gather` can be used to concurrently process multiple files inside of a directory hierarchy, as demonstrated here:\nL118: Python\nL119: \nL120:     `import asyncio\nL121:     import os\nL122:     import json\nL123:     import unstructured_client\nL124:     from unstructured_client.models import shared\nL125: \nL126:     client = unstructured_client.UnstructuredClient(\nL127:         api_key_auth=os.getenv(\"UNSTRUCTURED_API_KEY\")\nL128:     )\nL129: \nL130:     async def call_api(filename, input_dir, output_dir):\nL131:         req = {\nL132:             \"partition_parameters\": {\nL133:                 \"files\": {\nL134:                     \"content\": open(filename, \"rb\"),\nL135:                     \"file_name\": os.path.basename(filename),\nL136:                 },\nL137:                 \"strategy\": shared.Strategy.VLM,\nL138:                 \"vlm_model\": \"gpt-4o\",\nL139:                 \"vlm_model_provider\": \"openai\",\nL140:                 \"languages\": ['eng'],\nL141:                 \"split_pdf_page\", True,            # If True, splits the PDF file into smaller chunks of pages.\nL142:                 \"split_pdf_allow_failed\": True,    # If True, the partitioning continues even if some pages fail.\nL143:                 \"split_pdf_concurrency_level\": 15  # Set the number of concurrent request to the maximum value: 15.\nL144:             }\nL145:         }\nL146: \nL147:         try:\nL148:             res = await client.general.partition_async(\nL149:                 request=req\nL150:             )\nL151:             element_dicts = [element for element in res.elements]\nL152:             json_elements = json.dumps(element_dicts, indent=2)\nL153: \nL154:             # Create the output directory structure.\nL155:             relative_path = os.path.relpath(os.path.dirname(filename), input_dir)\nL156:             output_subdir = os.path.join(output_dir, relative_path)\nL157:             os.makedirs(output_subdir, exist_ok=True)\nL158: \nL159:             # Write the output file.\nL160:             output_filename = os.path.join(output_subdir, os.path.basename(filename) + \".json\")\nL161:             with open(output_filename, \"w\") as file:\nL162:                 file.write(json_elements)\nL163: \nL164:         except Exception as e:\nL165:             print(f\"Error processing {filename}: {e}\")\nL166: \nL167:     async def process_files(input_directory, output_directory):\nL168:         tasks = []\nL169: \nL170:         for root, _, files in os.walk(input_directory):\nL171:             for file in files:\nL172:                 if not file.endswith('.json'):\nL173:                     full_path = os.path.join(root, file)\nL174:                     tasks.append(call_api(full_path, input_directory, output_directory))\nL175: \nL176:         await asyncio.gather(*tasks)\nL177: \nL178:     if __name__ == \"__main__\":\nL179:         asyncio.run(process_files(\nL180:             input_directory=os.getenv(\"LOCAL_FILE_INPUT_DIR\"),\nL181:             output_directory=os.getenv(\"LOCAL_FILE_OUTPUT_DIR\")\nL182:         ))\nL183:     `\nL184: ##\nL185: \nL186: cite24†​ L187: \nL188: Page splitting\nL189: In order to speed up processing of large PDF files, the `split_pdf_page`cite25†* parameter is `True` by default. This causes the PDF to be split into small batches of pages before sending requests to the API. The client awaits all parallel requests and combines the responses into a single response object. This is specific to PDF files and other filetypes are ignored. The number of parallel requests is controlled by `split_pdf_concurrency_level`cite25†* .\n"
  }
]

Recent advances in document image analysis (DIA) have been primarily driven by the application of neural networks. Ideally, research outcomes could be easily deployed in production and extended for further investigation.\nL180: However, various factors like loosely organized codebases and sophisticated model conﬁgurations complicate the easy reuse of im- portant innovations by a wide audience. Though there have been on-going eﬀorts to improve reusability and simplify deep learning (DL) model development in disciplines like natural language processing and computer vision, none of them are optimized for challenges in the domain of DIA.\nL181: This represents a major gap in the existing toolkit, as DIA is central to academic research across a wide range of disciplines in the social sciences and humanities. This paper introduces LayoutParser, an open-source library for streamlining the usage of DL in DIA research and applica- tions. The core LayoutParser library comes with a set of simple and intuitive interfaces for applying and customizing DL models for layout de- tection, character recognition, and many other document processing tasks.\nL182: To promote extensibility, LayoutParser also incorporates a community platform for sharing both pre-trained models and full document digiti- zation pipelines. We demonstrate that LayoutParser is helpful for both lightweight and large-scale digitization pipelines in real-word use cases. `UnstructuredFileLoader` and others did. It instead supports “chunking”. Chunking in unstructured differs from other chunking mechanisms you may be familiar with that form chunks based on plain-text features—character sequences like “\\n\\n” or “\\n” that might indicate a paragraph boundary or list-item boundary.\nL311: Instead, all documents are split using specific knowledge about each document format to partition the document into semantic units (document elements) and we only need to resort to text-splitting when a single element exceeds the desired maximum chunk size. In general, chunking combines consecutive elements to form chunks as large as possible without exceeding the maximum chunk size. Chunking produces a sequence of CompositeElement, Table, or TableChunk elements.\nL312: Each “chunk” is an instance of one of these three types. Environment variables take precedence over `.env`. Keep `.env` private; it is excluded by `.gitignore`.\r\n\r\nParsing is local by default. To use the hosted **Unstructured Partition API**, set both `UNSTRUCTURED_API_KEY` and `UNSTRUCTURED_API_URL` in `.env`. If `UNSTRUCTURED_API_URL` is incompatible, the UI warns and uses local parsing instead; clear the URL in `.env` to remove the warning.\r\n\r\n## Run\r\n\r\nLegacy DOC parsing requires LibreOffice (`soffice`) on PATH. DOCX does not require LibreOffice. Start the app:\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\nstreamlit run app.py\r\n```\r\n\r\nOpen the local address Streamlit prints. Upload files, select **Build Index**, enter a question, then select **Ask**. Use **Reset** to delete the active collection.\r\n\r\n## Architecture\r\n\r\n```text\r\nUpload â†’ Pydantic validation â†’ Unstructured elements â†’ by_title chunks\r\n       â†’ Gemini embeddings â†’ ephemeral Chroma collection\r\nQuestion â†’ explicit top-K retrieval â†’ Gemini Flash answer\r\n         â†’ validated evidence IDs â†’ trusted citation metadata + passages\r\n```\r\n\r\nThe Streamlit UI stores the active index, parsed elements, chunks, and latest answer in session state. Building a replacement set creates a new collection before retiring the old one. Retrieval only searches the active collection, so old and new documents do not mix. Core pipeline steps stay outside `app.py`. Parsing uses the local Unstructured library unless a compatible Partition API key and URL are both configured.\r\n\r\n## Supported formats\r\n\r\nPDF (`.pdf`), UTF-8 TXT (`.txt`), Markdown (`.md`, `.markdown`), Word (`.doc`, `.docx`), and CSV (`.csv`). Upload up to 10 files per set, each up to 10 MiB; the resulting set is limited to 200 chunks by default. PDF page numbers are kept when Unstructured provides them. PDF table detection uses its high-resolution strategy and may download layout models or require local PDF tools. Legacy DOC requires LibreOffice.\r\n\r\nFor PDF OCR and table-aware extraction, install the **Tesseract OCR executable** separately from Python packages. On Windows, one option is:\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\nwinget install --id UB-Mannheim.TesseractOCR --exact\r\ntesseract --version\r\n```\r\n\r\nRestart the terminal and Streamlit after installation so the updated PATH is visible. The `unstructured[pdf]` dependency installs a Python wrapper, not the Tesseract executable. If Tesseract is unavailable, the app retries text-based PDFs with Unstructured's `fast` strategy and warns that table structure may be incomplete. Scanned PDFs without embedded text still need OCR and receive a clear setup error.\r\n\r\n## Project map\r\n\r\n```text\r\napp.py                    Streamlit entry point\r\ndocument_rag/\r\n retrieval.py            question-to-evidence retrieval\r\n  generation.py           grounded Gemini answers and citation validation\r\n  evaluation.py           rule-based local evaluation runner\r\n  ui.py                   Streamlit interface and debug views\r\ntests/                    credential-free contract tests\r\nevaluation/               local synthetic documents and question expectations\r\n\"\"\"Upload validation and Unstructured parsing behavior.\"\"\"\r\n\r\nfrom io import BytesIO\r\nfrom types import SimpleNamespace\r\n\r\nimport pytest\r\nfrom pydantic import UploadedDocument(BaseModel):\r\n    \"\"\"A file received from the Streamlit uploader.\"\"\"\r\n\r\n    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)\r\n\r\n    filename: str = Field(min_length=1)\r\n    content: bytes = Field(min_length=1, repr=False)\r\n\r\n    @model_validator(mode=\"after\")\r\n    def validate_type(self) -> \"UploadedDocument\":\r\n        if keep scores separate from vector distances.\"\"\"\n+    terms = set(tokenize(query))\n+    if not terms or not index.chunks:\n+        return []\n+    size = len(index.chunks)\n+    average_length = index.average_length or 1.0\n+    matches: list[tuple[DocumentChunk, float]] = []\n+    for chunk, frequencies, length in zip(index.chunks, index.frequencies, index.lengths):\n+        score = 0.0\n+        for term in terms:\n+            frequency = frequencies.get(term, 0)\n+            if not frequency:\n+                continue\n+            document_frequency = index.document_frequency[term]\n+            inverse_frequency = log(1 + (size - document_frequency + 0.5) / (document_frequency + 0.5))\n+            score += inverse_frequency * (frequency * 2.2) / (\n+                frequency + 1.2 * (0.25 + 0.75 * length / average_length)\n+            )\n+        if score > 0:\n+            matches.append((chunk, score))\n+    return sorted(matches, key=lambda item: (-item[1], item[0].chunk_id))[:limit]\n*** Add File: D:\\Projects\\Document-RAG\\document_rag\\reranking.py\n+\"\"\"Lazy local cross-encoder scoring for hybrid retrieval candidates.\"\"\"\n+\n+from functools import lru_cache\n+\n+\n+@lru_cache(maxsize=2)\n+def get_cross_encoder(model_name: str):\n+    from sentence_transformers import CrossEncoder\n+\n+    return CrossEncoder(model_name)\n+\n+\n+def rerank_scores(model_name: str, question: str, passages: list[str]) -> list[float]:\n+    if not passages:\n+        return []\n+    scores = get_cross_encoder(model_name).predict(\n+        [(question, passage) for passage in passages],\n+        show_progress_bar=False,\n+    )\n+    return [float(score) for score in scores]\n*** End Patch"));

```text
Yes. The app now combines Chroma and BM25 candidates, scores the combined set with a cross encoder, and applies `TOP_K` **after** reranking. Only those final passages go to Gemini. If the reranker cannot load, `TOP_K` applies to the hybrid ranking instead. [Sentence Transformers documents this reranking pattern.](https://www.sbert.net/docs/cross_encoder/usage/usage.html)

The change is in [retrieval.py](D:/Projects/Document-RAG/document_rag/retrieval.py); the UI shows the ranking scores. **71 tests pass.** The real cross encoder model download stalled in this environment, so I could verify its integration with mocked scores, but not a live model run. The app will warn and use hybrid ranking if that download fails.
```

## 918. Assistant

```text
Yes, that’s a reasonable choice for this app. Each Build Index creates a fresh in-memory collection for the current upload set, and citations point to passages in that active set. Reset or process restart removes the index, so persistent document version tracking adds little value.

Keep the existing document and chunk IDs to identify evidence within a session. Version tracking becomes useful if you later save indexes, retain past uploads, or need to reproduce an answer after the session ends.
```

plan_queries(\n+    question: str,\n+    config: AppConfig,\n+    max_subqueries: int,\n+    *,\n+    model: Any | None = None,\n+) -> list[str]:\n+    \"\"\"Return the original query followed by structured.invoke(\n+        [\n+            SystemMessage(content=_SYSTEM_PROMPT),\n+            HumanMessage(content=f\"Maximum subqueries: {max_subqueries}\\nQuestion: {original}\"),\n+        ]\n+    )\n+    plan = QueryPlan.model_validate(raw)\n+    queries = [original]\n+    seen = {original.casefold()}\n+    for candidate in plan.subqueries:\n+        if not isinstance(candidate, str):\n+ queries.append(subquery)\n+        seen.add(subquery.casefold())\n+        if len(queries) > max_subqueries:\n+            break\n+    return queries\n*** End Patch"));

For answers it checks inline citation IDs, their mapped chunk IDs and metadata against retrieved results, expected abstention, and literal answer keywords. Unanswerable questions have no retrieval hit expectation because a vector search still returns nearby passages. These rule-based checks do not establish semantic correctness. ## 963. Assistant

```text
Added query decomposition for multipart questions. The app keeps the original question, generates up to three focused search queries, searches the active document set with Chroma and BM25, then reranks the combined passages against the original question before applying `TOP_K`.

Simple questions skip the extra Gemini call. If planning fails, retrieval uses the original question. The Debug panel shows the queries used. A live comparison produced separate annual leave and sick leave queries, and **75 tests pass**. Decomposition broadens the evidence search; it does not guarantee that every answer improves.

## 974. Assistant

```text
The form layout does not submit the typed value correctly in Streamlit’s UI test harness, so I’m using the simpler interaction: Ask stays enabled whenever chunks are ready, and a click validates the question. That removes the typing and rerun dependency without changing how the answer pipeline runs.
```

```text

I’ll put the question and each passage into labeled JSON fields, strengthen the system instructions, and keep citation IDs tied to the trusted retrieval results.

The original question is always searched, and a planner failure falls back to that original question. Simple questions skip the planning call. The Debug panel shows the queries used. Planning adds one Gemini call for multipart questions; it never reads the uploaded documents or writes the answer.\n+\n+The query planner receives its task in a system instruction. The user's question is supplied as labeled, JSON-encoded input. Instruction-like text inside the question cannot be promoted to a system instruction by changing delimiters.\n@@\n `generate_answer` takes a question and retrieved results; it does not perform retrieval. It labels the supplied passages `[S1]`, `[S2]`, and so on, then asks Gemini Flash for a Pydantic response with `answer`, `evidence_ids`, and `insufficient_evidence`. It rejects unknown or inconsistent IDs and maps valid IDs to the source filename, page, section, chunk ID, and passage text supplied by retrieval. Gemini does not provide citation metadata to the final result.\n+\n+Gemini receives answer rules in a system message. The question and each retrieved passage are separate JSON fields; every passage is labeled `UNTRUSTED DOCUMENT CONTENT`. Passage text and metadata are never inserted into the system instruction. This boundary and the citation checks reduce prompt injection risk, but no prompt delimiter can guarantee that a model will ignore every malicious instruction in a document.\n*** End Patch"));

client=active_client,\\r\\n        store=store,\\r\\n        collection_name=name,\\r\\n        chunk_count=len(items),\\r\\n        retrieval_top_k=settings.retrieval_top_k,\\r\\n        lexical_index=lexical_index,\\r\\n    )\\r\\n    if previous_index is not None:\\r\\n        try:\\r\\n            reset_index(previous_index)\\r\\n        except Exception:\\r\\n            _delete_collection(active_client, name)\\r\\n            index.ready = False\\r\\n            raise\\r\\n    return index\\r\\n\\r\\n\\r\\ndef is_index_ready(index: VectorIndex | None) -> bool:\\r\\n
