On Windows PowerShell:\\r\\n\\r\\n```powershell\\r\\npy -3.12 -m venv .venv\\r\\n.\\\\.venv\\\\Scripts\\\\Activate.ps1\\r\\npython -m pip install --upgrade pip\\r\\npython -m pip install -r requirements.txt\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Configuration (.env)\\r\\n\\r\\nCopy the example file, then set your Google AI Studio API key:\\r\\n\\r\\n```powershell\\r\\nCopy-Item .env.example .env\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nSet `GOOGLE_API_KEY` in `.env` before building an index. `GEMINI_MODEL` defaults to `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, `GEMINI_EMBEDDING_MODEL` to `gemini-embedding-2`, and `TOP_K` to 5. Environment variables take precedence over `.env`. Keep `.env` private; it is excluded by `.gitignore`.\\r\\n\\r\\nParsing is local by default. To use the hosted **Unstructured Partition API**, set both `UNSTRUCTURED_API_KEY` and `UNSTRUCTURED_API_URL` in `.env`. The URL must be the Partition endpoint base URL or its full `/general/v0/general` URL from your Unstructured account. With both values set, uploaded documents are sent to that service; local Tesseract is then unnecessary. A key by itself leaves local parsing active. The Unstructured **Transform** web URL (`transform.unstructured.io/api/v2`) is a different product endpoint and does not work with the Partition API client. If `UNSTRUCTURED_API_URL` is incompatible, the UI warns and uses local parsing instead; clear the URL in `.env` to remove the warning.\\r\\n\\r\\nHosted parsing uses [`langchain_unstructured.UnstructuredLoader`](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/integrations/document_loaders/unstructured_file) with `partition_via_api=True`. For the standard Partition service, configure:\\r\\n\\r\\n```dotenv\\r\\nUNSTRUCTURED_API_KEY=your-partition-api-key\\r\\nUNSTRUCTURED_API_URL=https://api.unstructuredapp.io/general/v0/general\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nThe hostname is `api.unstructuredapp.io`. A connection error can indicate DNS, proxy, or TLS problems; HTTP 401 means the service rejected the key. A Transform key does not establish access to the legacy Partition endpoint. Restart Streamlit after changing `.env`, since previously loaded environment values take precedence. Hosted uploads use temporary files that are deleted after loading, including when parsing fails. The loader returns individual elements; filenames, pages, sections, and table HTML are retained for the existing chunking pipeline.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf the Partition API returns 401, the app parses the uploaded set locally and displays a warning. It sends no further files from that set to the rejected endpoint. To avoid the failed API request on each new build, leave `UNSTRUCTURED_API_URL` empty until you have a valid Partition API key. Local parsing of scanned PDFs still requires Tesseract OCR.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Run\\r\\n\\r\\nLegacy DOC parsing requires LibreOffice (`soffice`) on PATH. DOCX does not require LibreOffice. Start the app:\\r\\n\\r\\n```powershell\\r\\nstreamlit run app.py\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nOpen the local address Streamlit prints. Upload one or more files, select **Process Documents**, enter a question in the multiline question area, then select **Ask Question**. Questions use the active index even if the uploader selection changes; select **Process Documents** to replace it with the newly selected files. Use **Reset** to delete the active collection.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Architecture\\r\\n\\r\\n```text\\r\\nUpload â†’ Pydantic validation â†’ Unstructured elements â†’ by_title chunks\\r\\n       â†’ Gemini embeddings â†’ ephemeral Chroma collection\\r\\nQuestion â†’ optional query decomposition â†’ Chroma + BM25 per query\\r\\n         â†’ reciprocal rank fusion â†’ cross encoder â†’ top K â†’ Gemini Flash answer\\r\\n         â†’ validated evidence IDs â†’ trusted citation metadata + passages\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nThe Streamlit UI stores the active index, parsed elements, chunks, and latest answer in session state. Building a replacement set creates a new collection before retiring the old one. Retrieval only searches the active collection, so old and new documents do not mix. Core pipeline steps stay outside `app.py`. Parsing uses the local Unstructured library unless a compatible Partition API key and URL are both configured.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Supported formats\\r\\n\\r\\nPDF (`.pdf`), UTF-8 TXT (`.txt`), Markdown (`.md`, `.markdown`), Word (`.doc`, `.docx`), and CSV (`.csv`). Upload up to 10 files per set, each up to 10 MiB; the resulting set is limited to 200 chunks by default. PDF page numbers are kept when Unstructured provides them. PDF table detection uses its high-resolution strategy and may download layout models or require local PDF tools. Legacy DOC requires LibreOffice.\\r\\n\\r\\nFor PDF OCR and table-aware extraction, install the **Tesseract OCR executable** separately from Python packages. On Windows, one option is:\\r\\n\\r\\n```powershell\\r\\nwinget install --id UB-Mannheim.TesseractOCR --exact\\r\\ntesseract --version\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nRestart the terminal and Streamlit after installation so the updated PATH is visible. The `unstructured[pdf]` dependency installs a Python wrapper, not the Tesseract executable. If Tesseract is unavailable, the app retries text-based PDFs with Unstructured's `fast` strategy and warns that table structure may be incomplete. Scanned PDFs without embedded text still need OCR and receive a clear setup error.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Project map\\r\\n\\r\\n```text\\r\\napp.py                    Streamlit entry point\\r\\ndocument_rag/\\r\\n  config.py               .env loading and validated settings\\r\\n  models.py               shared Pydantic contracts\\r\\n  parsing.py              Upload validation and Unstructured extraction\\r\\n  chunking.py             section-aware prose and table chunking\\r\\n  embeddings.py           Gemini embedding adapter\\r\\n  vector_store.py         in-memory Chroma lifecycle and search\\r\\n  lexical.py              in-memory BM25 index for the active document set\\r\\n  query_planning.py       bounded Gemini query decomposition\\r\\n  retrieval.py            hybrid candidate fusion and top-K selection\\r\\n  reranking.py            cached local cross encoder\\r\\n  generation.py           grounded Gemini answers and citation validation\\r\\n  evaluation.py           rule-based local evaluation runner\\r\\n  ui.py                   Streamlit interface and debug views\\r\\ntests/                    credential-free contract tests\\r\\nevaluation/               local synthetic documents and question expectations\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Using the app\\r\\n\\r\\nUpload multiple PDF, TXT, Markdown, DOC, DOCX, or CSV files in the sidebar and select **Process Documents**. Once chunks are ready, **Ask Question** is enabled. Enter a question to see a grounded answer, citations, and supporting passages. A blank question shows a prompt to enter text. Expand **Debug** to inspect parsed elements, chunks, retrieved passages, cosine distances, BM25 and rerank scores, and source metadata.\\r\\n\\r\\nChanging the selected files does not interrupt questions against the active index. A successful **Process Documents** action creates a fresh collection and deletes the previous one; if it fails, the previous collection remains available. **Reset** deletes the active collection and clears answer and debug data. Session state keeps the index across reruns. Restarting the Python process discards all in-memory indexes; losing a browser session loses its index reference.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Parsing API\\r\\n\\r\\n`parse_documents` accepts a list of `UploadedDocument` values and returns one `ParsedDocument` per source. Supported extensions are `.pdf`, `.txt`, `.md`, `.markdown`, `.doc`, `.docx`, and `.csv`. Each document contains ordered `ParsedElement` values with a stable source ID, source filename, element type, page number when available, and the current section title. Table elements keep Unstructured's HTML and extracted header cells when available. CSV uses its first row as headers; Word tables retain their text and HTML structure when Unstructured provides it.\\r\\n\\r\\n```python\\r\\nfrom document_rag.models import UploadedDocument\\r\\nfrom document_rag.parsing import parse_documents\\r\\n\\r\\ndocuments = parse_documents([\\r\\n    UploadedDocument(filename=\\\"notes.md\\\", content=b\\\"# Notes\\\\n\\\\nA fact.\\\"),\\r\\n    UploadedDocument(filename=\\\"memo.txt\\\", content=b\\\"Another fact.\\\"),\\r\\n])\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nThe validator rejects unsupported extensions, empty or whitespace-only files, non-UTF-8 TXT/Markdown/CSV files, duplicate filenames, and uploads over the configured file count or byte limit. A file that yields no usable elements is rejected after parsing. Extracted elements remain grouped by source. Legacy DOC conversion may use temporary files inside Unstructured.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Chunking API\\r\\n\\r\\nPass parsed documents to `chunk_documents` to get bounded `DocumentChunk` values. Prose is grouped within each section and page using Unstructured's `by_title` chunker. Each chunk's text includes its section heading, and the same text is available as `embedding_text`. Tables are kept separate; their headers are repeated when rows span multiple chunks. Chunk IDs are deterministic for a source and do not depend on the order of other uploaded files.\\r\\n\\r\\n```python\\r\\nfrom document_rag.chunking import chunk_documents\\r\\n\\r\\nchunks = chunk_documents(documents)\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nDefaults are a 2,000-character hard limit, 1,400-character target, and 80-character minimum used to rebalance short trailing prose. A standalone short fact is kept rather than discarded. Title-only documents and inputs exceeding the configured 200-chunk limit raise `ChunkingError`.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Vector index API\\r\\n\\r\\n`build_index` creates a new collection in `chromadb.EphemeralClient()` and stores each chunk's text plus its source, page, heading, type, and ID metadata. The embedding adapter uses `GoogleGenerativeAIEmbeddings` with `gemini-embedding-2`. Search returns ranked `RetrievedChunk` values; distances are vector distances, not confidence scores.\\r\\n\\r\\n```python\\r\\nfrom document_rag.vector_store import build_index, is_index_ready, reset_index, search_index\\r\\n\\r\\nindex = build_index(chunks)\\r\\nif is_index_ready(index):\\r\\n    hits = search_index(index, \\\"What does the document say?\\\", top_k=5)\\r\\nreset_index(index)\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nTo replace a dataset, call `build_index(new_chunks, previous_index=index)`. The new collection becomes ready before the old collection is deleted. If building fails, the old index remains available. Each collection is isolated and lost when the Python process exits; no Chroma persistence directory is used.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Retrieval API\\r\\n\\r\\nFor questions that appear to ask about multiple topics, Gemini Flash-Lite creates up to `MAX_SUBQUERIES=3` short search queries. `QUERY_DECOMPOSITION_ENABLED=true` controls this step. The original question is always searched, and a planner failure falls back to that original question. Simple questions skip the planning call. The Debug panel shows the queries used. Planning adds one Gemini call for multipart questions; it never reads the uploaded documents or writes the answer.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe query planner receives its task in a system instruction. The user's question is supplied as labeled, JSON-encoded input. Instruction-like text inside the question cannot be promoted to a system instruction by changing delimiters.\\r\\n\\r\\n`retrieve` searches Chroma and the active set's in-memory BM25 index for each query, merges candidates by reciprocal rank fusion, then scores those candidates against the **original question** with a local `cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2` model. `TOP_K` is applied **after** reranking, so only the highest ranked passages reach Gemini. `RETRIEVAL_CANDIDATES` defaults to 20 and is divided across the planned queries, with at least `TOP_K` candidates from each search method per query; `RERANK_ENABLED=true` and `RERANK_MODEL` configure the reranker. The model downloads on the first Ask and is cached in the Python process. If it cannot load, the app warns and uses hybrid ranking. The first download can be prepared ahead of time with `python -c \\\"from sentence_transformers import CrossEncoder; CrossEncoder('cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2')\\\"`. It requires access to Hugging Face; this environment could not complete that download during verification. Each result retains its source metadata, vector distance when available, BM25 score when matched, fusion score, and rerank score when applied. These scores are ranking signals, not answer confidence. Retrieval does not call the answer model.\\r\\n\\r\\n```python\\r\\nfrom document_rag.retrieval import retrieve\\r\\n\\r\\nresults = retrieve(\\\"What does the report say about sales?\\\", index)\\r\\nfor result in results:\\r\\n    print(result.rank, result.source, result.page, result.text)\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nPass `top_k=...` for a one-call override, or set `TOP_K` in `.env`. Empty questions and missing or reset indexes produce clear errors.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Answer generation API\\r\\n\\r\\n`generate_answer` takes a question and retrieved results; it does not perform retrieval. It labels the supplied passages `[S1]`, `[S2]`, and so on, then asks Gemini Flash for a Pydantic response with `answer`, `evidence_ids`, and `insufficient_evidence`. It rejects unknown or inconsistent IDs and maps valid IDs to the source filename, page, section, chunk ID, and passage text supplied by retrieval. Gemini does not provide citation metadata to the final result.\\r\\n\\r\\nGemini receives answer rules in a system message. The question and each retrieved passage are separate JSON fields; every passage is labeled `UNTRUSTED DOCUMENT CONTENT`. Passage text and metadata are never inserted into the system instruction. This boundary and the citation checks reduce prompt injection risk, but no prompt delimiter can guarantee that a model will ignore every malicious instruction in a document.\\r\\n\\r\\n```python\\r\\nfrom document_rag.generation import generate_answer\\r\\nfrom document_rag.retrieval import retrieve\\r\\n\\r\\nresults = retrieve(\\\"How much annual leave is provided?\\\", index)\\r\\nanswer = generate_answer(\\\"How much annual leave is provided?\\\", results)\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nWith no retrieved evidence, or when Gemini says the evidence is insufficient, the function returns a standard abstention. Citation validation confirms that IDs refer to supplied passages; it cannot by itself prove every sentence is factually supported.\\r\\n\\r\\nSee [PLAN.md](PLAN.md) for the detailed implementation sequence, evaluation approach, and limitations.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Evaluation\\r\\n\\r\\nThe local [question fixture](evaluation/cases.json) pairs three synthetic documents with four answerable questions and one unanswerable question. Each answerable case specifies its source filename, optional page, and keywords expected together in a retrieved passage.\\r\\n\\r\\n```powershell\\r\\npython -m document_rag.evaluation --retrieval-only\\r\\npython -m document_rag.evaluation\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nBoth commands build a fresh in-memory index from the fixture and need a working Gemini embedding key. The second also calls Gemini Flash for answers. The runner prints JSON with each question's source presence in top K, source rank, first passage rank matching source/page/keywords, and hit@k; it then reports aggregate hit@k. For answers it checks inline citation IDs, their mapped chunk IDs and metadata against retrieved results, expected abstention, and literal answer keywords. Unanswerable questions have no retrieval hit expectation because a vector search still returns nearby passages. These rule-based checks do not establish semantic correctness. Tests in `tests/test_evaluation.py` use doubles and require no API key. You can change `--top-k` or point `--cases` to another local fixture with the same schema.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Testing\\r\\n\\r\\n```powershell\\r\\npython -m pytest -q\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nThe test suite covers validation, Unstructured parsing, section and table chunking, fake Gemini adapters, real ephemeral Chroma collections with fake embeddings, retrieval, mocked answer generation, UI lifecycle, dataset replacement, reset, and evaluation rules. It makes no Gemini API calls. Run the evaluation commands above separately when you want to measure the configured live models.\\r\\n\\r\\nTo exercise the actual Streamlit upload, build, Ask, citation, passage, and reset flow with your configured Gemini API key, run:\\r\\n\\r\\n```powershell\\r\\npython scripts/live_ui_smoke.py\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nThis smoke check makes real embedding and answer requests and may fail temporarily if Gemini returns 503. The UI reports that condition and keeps the index available for another Ask attempt.\\r\\n\\r\\nTo check the complete LangChain pipeline directly with the configured services, run:\\r\\n\\r\\n```powershell\\r\\npython scripts/live_pipeline_smoke.py\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nThis check verifies Gemini embedding dimensions, Unstructured parsing of two files, chunking, a nonpersistent LangChain Chroma collection with source metadata, hybrid retrieval and cross encoder scores, grounded Gemini output with citations, query decomposition, replacement without old document mixing, and reset. It makes live Gemini requests and may download the reranker model on first use.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Limitations\\r\\n\\r\\n- In-memory indexes disappear when the Python process ends. Losing a Streamlit session loses its index reference but may leave its collection in process memory until restart; use **Reset** before closing the session when possible. This is a local demo with no authentication or durable storage.\\r\\n- PDF high-resolution parsing can need Tesseract and additional local tools or model downloads. Without Tesseract, text PDFs use `fast` extraction, which may lose table structure or reading order; scanned PDFs cannot be parsed without OCR. Page numbers are shown only when Unstructured supplies them.\\r\\n- Hybrid search still returns nearby passages for unanswerable questions. Gemini is instructed to abstain; citation validation proves references point to retrieved chunks, not that every claim is factually supported.\\r\\n- The cross encoder needs a first-use model download and adds local CPU or GPU work to each question. It reranks candidates only; it cannot repair answer-model API errors.\\r\\n- The evaluation uses literal keywords and source/page checks. Correct paraphrases may fail its answer-keyword check; a passing check is not a semantic guarantee.\\r\\n- Indexing and answering require API access and available Gemini quota. The automated tests do not verify live model availability.\\r\\n- Hosted Unstructured parsing requires a compatible Partition API key and endpoint. Transform MCP credentials or web URLs are not interchangeable with the Partition API.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Future improvements\\r\\n\\r\\n- Add a reproducible live evaluation report with sample PDF pages and tables, including retrieval latency and failed cases.\\r\\n- Improve OCR and table handling for scanned or complex PDFs after measuring failures on representative documents.\\r\\n- Add clearer progress and recovery guidance for large uploads and external API errors.\\r\\n\\r\\n## References\\r\\n\\r\\n- [Ge…5847 tokens truncated….getenv(\\\"GEMINI_EMBEDDING_MODEL\\\", \\\"gemini-embedding-2\\\"),\\r\\n        retrieval_top_k=os.getenv(\\\"TOP_K\\\", \\\"5\\\"),\\r\\n        retrieval_candidate_pool=os.getenv(\\\"RETRIEVAL_CANDIDATES\\\", \\\"20\\\"),\\r\\n        query_decomposition_enabled=os.getenv(\\\"QUERY_DECOMPOSITION_ENABLED\\\", \\\"true\\\"),\\r\\n        max_subqueries=os.getenv(\\\"MAX_SUBQUERIES\\\", \\\"3\\\"),\\r\\n        rerank_enabled=os.getenv(\\\"RERANK_ENABLED\\\", \\\"true\\\"),\\r\\n        rerank_model=os.getenv(\\\"RERANK_MODEL\\\", \\\"cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2\\\"),\\r\\n    )\\r\\n\\r\\n\\r\\ndef unstructured_api_url_warning(value: str | None) -> str | None:\\r\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Explain why an environment URL cannot be used for hosted partitioning.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\r\\n    try:\\r\\n        AppConfig.blank_url_is_missing(value)\\r\\n    except ValueError:\\r\\n        return (\\r\\n            \\\"UNSTRUCTURED_API_URL is not a Partition API endpoint. \\\"\\r\\n            \\\"Using local Unstructured parsing. ````text
# Context from my IDE setup:

## Active file: README.md

## Active selection of the file:
# Document RAG

A Streamlit app that accepts documents at runtime, builds an in-memory index, and answers questions from uploaded evidence. Process a new document set to replace the active index without changing code.

## Features

- Upload multiple PDF, TXT, Markdown (`.md`, `.markdown`), DOC, DOCX, or CSV files. Validation rejects empty, unsupported, oversized, or excessive uploads.
- Parse with Unstructured, retaining filename, page, section/title, element type, and table context where available.
- Split prose with Unstructured `chunk_by_title`; include headings in chunk text and retain table headers with rows. Chunk IDs are deterministic.
- Embed with Gemini `gemini-embedding-2` and store text and metadata in an in-memory Chroma collection with cosine distance.
- Search with Chroma semantic retrieval and in-memory BM25, combine candidates with reciprocal rank fusion, then rerank with a local cross encoder. Select `TOP_K` after reranking.
- Optionally decompose comparison and multi-part questions into focused searches; also search the original question.
- Generate grounded Gemini Flash Lite answers with `[S1]` evidence citations, source metadata, supporting passages, and an insufficient-evidence response when needed.
- Inspect parsed elements, chunks, search queries, retrieval scores, and metadata in the Streamlit Debug section.
- Replace or reset the active document set. Each successful build uses a fresh Chroma collection, preventing old/new mixing.

## Technology decisions

**LangChain** connects Gemini embeddings, the answer model, and Chroma through standard components. Its document and model interfaces let filename, page, and section metadata travel through indexing and retrieval for citations. LangChain handles much of the model/vector-store wiring; explicit prompt messages and separate pipeline modules make the flow inspectable and let us compare chunking or retrieval settings without rewriting the app.

**Unstructured** extracts document elements and their structure across formats. `chunk_by_title` groups prose under section headings so meaning survives splitting. Table handling keeps headers with rows. This makes new runtime document sets usable without parser or chunking code changes.

**Hybrid retrieval helps find the right evidence; a cross encoder helps put the best evidence first.** BM25 finds exact terms, Chroma finds semantic matches, reciprocal rank fusion combines candidates, and the cross encoder scores them against the original question. `TOP_K` selects the best-ranked available passages after reranking. Scores are ranking signals, not answer-confidence estimates.

**Query decomposition** helps complex questions with comparisons or multiple tasks. A planner can produce up to `MAX_SUBQUERIES` focused queries; retrieval always includes the original question. If planning fails, retrieval continues with the original question.

## Install

Python 3.12 is recommended. From the project root, on Windows PowerShell:

```powershell
py -3.12 -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
Copy-Item .env.example .env
```

On macOS/Linux, create and activate the environment with `python3 -m venv .venv` and `source .venv/bin/activate`, then use the same pip commands and `cp .env.example .env`.

Scanned PDFs require Tesseract OCR; legacy `.doc` files may require LibreOffice. The first reranking run may download model weights from Hugging Face. Hosted Unstructured Partition is optional.

## Configure `.env`

Set `GOOGLE_API_KEY` in `.env`. Do not commit this file. Environment variables override `.env`; restart Streamlit after editing settings.

| Variable                      | Default                               | Purpose                                                                                             |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GOOGLE_API_KEY`              | Required                              | Gemini embeddings, planning, and answers.                                                           |
| `GEMINI_MODEL`                | `gemini-3.8-flash`                    | Model used for planning and answers; the key must have access.                                      |
| `GEMINI_EMBEDDING_MODEL`      | `gemini-embedding-2`                  | Embedding model; requested output is 768 dimensions.                                                |
| `TOP_K`                       | `5`                                   | Maximum final passages after reranking.                                                             |
| `RETRIEVAL_CANDIDATES`        | `20`                                  | Candidate-pool target before final selection; actual searches depend on query count and index size. |
| `QUERY_DECOMPOSITION_ENABLED` | `true`                                | Plan subqueries for composite questions.                                                            |
| `MAX_SUBQUERIES`              | `3`                                   | Maximum planned subquestions.                                                                       |
| `RERANK_ENABLED`              | `true`                                | Use local cross encoder reranking.                                                                  |
| `RERANK_MODEL`                | `cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2` | Sentence Transformers cross encoder.                                                                |
| `UNSTRUCTURED_API_KEY`        | Empty                                 | Optional hosted Unstructured Partition key.                                                         |
| `UNSTRUCTURED_API_URL`        | Empty                                 | Matching HTTPS Partition endpoint, required with hosted key.                                        |

For hosted parsing, use the Partition URL supplied with your Unstructured account, for example `https://api.unstructuredapp.io/general/v0/general`. The Transform URL `https://transform.unstructured.io/api/v2` is a different API. With no hosted key/URL, parsing runs locally. A hosted 401 may fall back to local parsing; other connection errors are reported.

`document_rag/config.py` also defines limits: 10 files, 10 MiB per file, 200 chunks, and chunk sizes of 2,000 maximum, 1,400 target, and 80 minimum characters. These `AppConfig` fields are not `.env` variables.

## Run and use

```powershell
python -m streamlit run app.py
```

1. Select one or more supported files in the sidebar and click **Process Documents**.
2. When the index has chunks, enter a question in the text area and click **Ask Question**.
3. Read the answer, citations, and supporting passages. Open **Debug** for parsed elements, chunks, search queries, scores, and metadata.
4. Select different files and click **Process Documents** to replace the set. A failed replacement keeps the previous working index. Click **Reset** to remove it.

Streamlit session state keeps the index across reruns. Chroma uses `EphemeralClient`; documents and vectors are not persisted and disappear when the session or process ends. Downloaded cross encoder model weights may be cached locally.

## Architecture

```text
Uploads -> validation -> Unstructured elements -> title/table-aware chunks
        -> Gemini embeddings -> in-memory Chroma
Question -> optional subqueries -> Chroma + BM25 -> rank fusion
         -> cross-encoder reranking -> TOP_K evidence
         -> Gemini structured answer -> validated citations
```

| Module                                                       | Responsibility                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `app.py`, `document_rag/ui.py`                               | Streamlit entry point, session state, upload/question UI, Debug view.    |
| `document_rag/config.py`, `document_rag/models.py`           | Pydantic settings and pipeline data.                                     |
| `document_rag/parsing.py`, `document_rag/chunking.py`        | Upload validation, Unstructured parsing, heading and table-aware chunks. |
| `document_rag/embeddings.py`, `document_rag/vector_store.py` | Gemini embeddings and isolated in-memory Chroma collections.             |
| `document_rag/lexical.py`, `document_rag/query_planning.py`  | BM25 and optional question decomposition.                                |
| `document_rag/retrieval.py`, `document_rag/reranking.py`     | Candidates, rank fusion, reranking, final selection.                     |
| `document_rag/generation.py`                                 | Evidence-only prompting, Pydantic output, citation validation.           |
| `document_rag/evaluation.py`, `evaluation/`                  | Local evaluation cases and metrics.                                      |
| `tests/`, `scripts/`                                         | Offline tests and optional live smoke checks.                            |

Prompts label user questions and retrieved passages as untrusted input. System instructions tell Gemini to answer only the user's question from supplied evidence. Code maps evidence IDs to actual retrieval metadata and rejects invalid citations. These measures reduce prompt-injection risk but cannot guarantee immunity.

## Test and evaluate

```powershell
python -m pytest -q
```

Tests use fake embeddings and mocked model responses, so they do not call Gemini. Optional live checks require `.env`, network access, and API quota:

```powershell
python scripts/live_pipeline_smoke.py
python scripts/live_ui_smoke.py
```

The small local evaluation measures expected source rank and hit@K, expected keywords, valid citations, and abstention without an LLM judge:

```powershell
python -m document_rag.evaluation --retrieval-only
python -m document_rag.evaluation
```

The offline suite (78 tests) and live pipeline/UI checks passed in the project environment on 2026-10-07. Live results depend on model availability, keys, network, and document content.

## Limitations and next steps

- The index is session-local and temporary; re-upload after restarting. There is no multi-user document store or version tracking.
- OCR and extraction quality depend on Tesseract, document structure, and parser output. Page or section metadata may be missing.
- Initial reranking may need network access for weights. If it is unavailable, retrieval falls back to hybrid ranking with a warning.
- Query decomposition adds a model call for qualifying questions, increasing latency and quota use.
- Citation checks verify IDs refer to retrieved passages; they do not prove every claim is fully supported. Review supporting passages for important decisions.
- Broader document evaluation would help tune chunk sizes, candidate counts, and reranker choice.

See [PLAN.md](PLAN.md) for implementation status and decisions.
